questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
What is least likely to happen if a firm decides to increase automation and division of labour in its production process?

options.A: an increase in cost per unit
options.C: an increase in the firm’s profits
options.D: an increase in the number of workers employed

questions.questionText: There is a fall in the world price of tea traded on wholesale international markets. How will this most likely affect the supply curve of a major tea retailer?

options.A: It will cause a contraction along the supply curve.
options.B: It will cause an extension along the supply curve.
options.C: It will cause the supply curve to shift to the left.
options.D: It will cause the supply curve to shift to the right.

questions.questionText: It was estimated in 2015 that milk had an income elasticity of demand of –0.6. What can be concluded about milk from this information?

options.A: It accounts for only a small proportion of household expenditure.
options.C: Household expenditure on milk will decrease if the price of milk increases.

A market is in an unstable disequilibrium when it does not return to its equilibrium point from a disequilibrium position. The diagram shows a market with two equilibrium points. At which price is the market in an unstable disequilibrium?

options.D: S price A B C D O quantity

questions.questionText: In which situation will it be necessary to use an alternative to the price mechanism to allocate a good between consumers?

options.A: Supply exceeds the quantity demanded at the initial market price.
options.B: The government sets a price ceiling below the equilibrium price.
options.C: The product is excludable and rival.
options.D: There is a single monopoly producer.

A market is in equilibrium at price $5. Market supply changes from being inelastic at each price to become elastic at each price. The market equilibrium price does not change. What is the effect on consumer surplus and producer surplus? consumer producer surplus surplus
A government has introduced an effective maximum price on rice. Which combination of changes must cause an existing shortage of rice to increase the most?

options.A: a fall in the maximum price and a less price-elastic supply
options.B: a fall in the maximum price and a more price-elastic supply
options.C: a rise in the maximum price and a less price-elastic supply
options.D: a rise in the maximum price and more price-elastic supply

What has happened when a country’s terms of trade are said to have moved in a favourable direction?

options.A: Each unit of imports costs more exports.
options.B: More foreign currency enters the country to pay for exports.
options.C: The monetary value of exports and imports is equalised.
options.D: The ratio of the index of export prices to the index of import prices increases.

questions.questionText: What is the least likely outcome for participating countries of a move towards freer trade?

options.B: a more equal distribution of income

What is a disadvantage when a quota replaces a tariff to reduce imports?

options.A: It is harder to anticipate its impact.
options.B: It is less effective at raising revenue for the government.
options.C: It is less effective when imports are necessities.
options.D: It prevents any involvement of market forces.

Suppose a country has a rate of inflation well below its target rate, high unemployment and a large balance of payments deficit. What would an economic advisor to the government be most likely to recommend?

options.A: a long-run supply side policy, aimed at improving the country’s efficiency, so improving both the unemployment and the balance of payments positions
options.B: a revaluation of its currency, because that would lead to reduced unemployment and an improved balance of payments
options.C: a rise in interest rates, because it would lead to an improved balance of payments and help achieve the inflation target
